parsed.why: Nationwide restroom law bars access by birth sex — tier-1 universal exposure; hate-crime protections repealed and trans-targeted hate crimes rising; one remedy took 20 years. No trans-specific offence, courts functioning, but no working recourse.

State itself hostile: passport/visa marker rules, screening refusals, transgender entry ban, counterterrorism 'pro-transgender' framing, documented custody abuse; facility bans across many states. Courts, hate-crime law and protections elsewhere only partly offset.

No criminalisation, no documented trans targeting or violence, but no anti-discrimination or hate-crime law, no recognition, LGBTQ people avoid police, and a dated port exclusion. Thin data resolves on those structural gaps.

Criminal code punishes public same-sex affection more heavily; local NGO documents police mistreatment and torture of LGBTQ people with no remedy; entrenched hostility, concealment, no protections. No visitor-facing facility or document rule documented.

Decriminalised 2023; sexual-orientation discrimination banned; police protected Pride, PM and religious leaders supportive, polls regionally favourable. Offset by Pride death threats, 2024 election hate speech, unregistrable LGBTI groups, hospital discrimination.
